newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Joetsu gets power generator licence.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Joetsu gets power generator licence.

text.p: Joetsu Co-operative Thermal Power Co Inc said on Friday it has acquired a licence as a power producer, enabling it to go ahead with plans to build a thermal power plant in Niigata, northern Japan, by 2011.
The proposed power plant would have three power generator lines with a total capacity of 3.97 million kilowatt (kw) and run on liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The plant is expected to use 3.42 million tonnes of LNG per year. Joetsu is owned equally by Chubu Electric Power Co Inc and Tohoku Electric Power Co Inc, who will choose fuel suppliers for Joetsu, a Joetsu spokesman said.
The first line, with output capacity of 1.27 million kw, is scheduled to start operations by July 2005, followed by the startup of the second line, of equal capacity, by July 2006.
The third line, with generation capability of 1.44 million kw, will start operations by 2011.
The spokesman said electricity from the plant will be provided to Chubu Electric and Tohoku Electric, which supply electricity to parts of northern and central Japan.
He said the estimated cost of constructing the facilities was 800 billion yen.
